title: Bless You, Forty-One
subject: a woman in hay-fever season who secretly keeps count of how many times her boyfriend says bless you, and realises on the forty-first sneeze of April that he has never once missed one
caption: Orchestral jazz-pop in a vintage crooner style. Close-miked string quartet playing lush legato chords, nylon-string guitar with soft bossa-leaning comping, walking upright bass, twinkling celesta on the turnarounds, light brushed drums. Warm vintage room sound with soft tape hiss. Female alto, low and velvety, conversational with a smile in it. 84 BPM, Bb major. Tender, wry and lovestruck. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM, no belted pop runs, no rock guitar.
lyrics:
[Intro - strings and celesta]

[Verse 1]
The birch trees out on Elm Street
Have it in for me again
I sneeze into my sleeve
You say bless you from the den

[Pre-Chorus]
I started keeping score
On the back of my hand

[Chorus]
Bless you, thirty-nine
Bless you, forty too
Every single time
It comes from you

[Verse 2]
You say it with your mouth full
You say it half asleep
You said it through the shower door
Without missing a beat

[Pre-Chorus]
I wasn't counting love
I was counting tissues

[Chorus]
Bless you, forty-one
Muffled through the wall
I think I've been blessed
More than I recall

[Bridge - strings swell]
Let the pollen fall all May
I'll let you keep the count

[Outro - nylon guitar alone]
Achoo
Bless you, love
